content.text: flop (flɒp ) Word forms: plural, 3rd person singular present tense flops , present participle flopping , past tense, past participle flopped 1. intransitive verb If you flop into a chair, for example, you sit down suddenly and heavily because you are so tired. Bunbury flopped down upon the bed and rested his tired feet. 2. intransitive verb If something flops onto something else, it falls there heavily or untidily. The briefcase flopped onto the desk. 3. intransitive verb If something flops, it is completely unsuccessful. [informal] The movie flopped badly at the box office. 4. countable noun If something is a flop, it is completely unsuccessful. [informal] It is the public who decide whether a movie is a hit or a flop. Collins COBUILD Advanced Learner’s Dictionary. Copyright © HarperCollins Publishers American English pronunciation ! Derived forms flopper (ˈflopper) noun flop in American English (flɑp) (verb flopped, flopping) intransitive verb1. (sometimes fol. by down) to fall or plump down suddenly, esp. with noise; drop or turn with a sudden bump or thud The puppy flopped down on the couch 2. (often fol. by over) to change suddenly, as from one side or party to another 3. to be a complete failure; fail The play flopped dismally 4. informal to flop at a friend's house 5. His long hair flops in his eyes when he runs transitive verb6. to drop with a sudden bump or thud I flopped my books on a chair 7. to flop oneself in a chair noun 10. the sound of flopping; a thud 11. a failure The new comedy was a flop 12. informal The mission offered a flop and a free breakfast SYNONYMS 11. fiasco, disaster, debacle; bomb, dog.Most material © 2005, 1997, 1991 by Penguin Random House LLC.
